name: Mondrian Hong Kong
positioning: Art-led design hotel in Tsim Sha Tsui, the first Mondrian hotel in Greater China, with Victoria Harbour and skyline views
best_for: Design and art lovers who want cultural programming on site
Travelers who want a Tsim Sha Tsui base with Victoria Harbour views

facts.text: Mondrian Hong Kong is in the Tsim Sha Tsui district, with quick access to key attractions and landmarks.
Mondrian Hong Kong is the first Mondrian hotel in Greater China.
The hotel occupies a tall, slender tower with triangular windows that previously housed the Panorama Hotel.
The rooms reimagine heritage design motifs through a contemporary lens, against the backdrop of Victoria Harbour and the Hong Kong skyline.
Rooms connect to the city's spirit through nuanced designs, local art and Victoria Harbour views.
Rooms feature washi-paper lamps, custom graphic rugs and bold hits of crimson and mustard.
The Harbour Suite has a lounge area, a connecting bedroom and two washrooms, one with a bathtub.
The Cornershop art space is open to the public daily, free of charge, with no reservation required.
The hotel regularly hosts cultural programmes, live music, DJ nights, brand collaborations and art-led experiences throughout the year.
Kowloon Park is a five-minute walk from the hotel.
Carna by Dario Cecchini is a contemporary Italian steak restaurant led by butcher Dario Cecchini, focused on premium cuts and nose-to-tail dining.
Avoca, on the 38th floor, serves creative cocktails and all-day dining.

highlights.text: The open-air Roofgarden offers views of Victoria Harbour and the Hong Kong skyline, a spot for sunrise, sunset or the city lights after dark.
The Cornershop, a street-level space opposite the hotel, is dedicated to artistic pop-up experiences.
The lobby has a two-story-high mosaic of underwater dancers and an orbital chandelier.
The Harbour Suite offers 180-degree views of the harbour or the Hong Kong cityscape through oversized windows.
Amsterdam-based designer Karin Krautgartner and her studio byKK transformed the interiors with bold, saturated hues.

considerations.text: The hotel does not have a spa or wellness centre.
The hotel does not have a swimming pool.
WhataHotel notes compact room sizes typical of Hong Kong properties.
